items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: When you listen to the way Charlie Rouse for example, plays Monk’s melodies with him

ctx.x: Yeah and if you haven’t done it well you have to be careful not to blame the players. Like that’s not supposed to sound that way what are you doing.

Well sometimes that is an issue. You know? Like I’m very detail oriented. I’m very specific the way I perceive of a melody, the way I conceive of a melody for example, or the phrasing of any phrase, the articulation of a phrase. The way I would play it on the piano, the way I conceive it is how I want it. And when you notate something for another musician, a horn player for example, if you’re going to put articulation markings they must be observed. You don’t want them to be ignored. But there are so many…

to learn the songs for the first time on the bandstand at the Five Spot. And Monk would just play the melody over and over again until he got it. But once he got it it was as pure as Monk’s intent could be because there is no other type of interpretation, here it is. Copy that.
